svg.text: THE TWO CALIFORNIAS · 1804
PROVINCIA DE LA NUEVA CALIFORNIA · PROVINCIA DE LA ANTIGUA CALIFORNIA · ordered 1804, effected 1806 · the threads that still tied them together
THE CROWN
King of Spain · wills the division (real orden, 1804)
Viceroy of New Spain
since 1793 BOTH Californias answer straight to him;
one Habilitado General in Mexico City still handles
BOTH provinces' pay & supply (C-A 16 d562)
ALTA (NUEVA) CALIFORNIA
BAJA (ANTIGUA) CALIFORNIA
GOVERNOR of Alta California
José Joaquín de Arrillaga 1804–14 · Pablo Vicente de Solá 1815–21
seat: MONTEREY (Arrillaga worked from San Diego
through the 1806 handover · C-A 25 d587)
keeps: 4 presidios · the Franciscan missions · 3 pueblos
GOVERNOR of Baja California
Felipe de Goycoechea 1806–14 · J. D. Argüello 1815–21 (→ de la Toba)
seat: LORETO · sworn in Mexico (Aug 1806, C-A 14 d452),
recognized by the Comandante of Loreto 5 Jul 1806 (C-A 25 d570)
keeps: the Loreto presidio · the Dominican missions · the frontier
LA LÍNEA DIVISORIA
the Arroyo del Rosario, alias "Barrabás," between San Diego
and Dominican Mission San Miguel · fixed by the padres of both
orders + the Comandante de la Frontera (C-A 25 d587, Dec 1806);
it simply ratifies the 1772 Franciscan–Dominican order
boundary (C-A 62 d19) · the church line became the state line
4 PRESIDIOS (Alta)
San Diego · Santa Bárbara · Monterey · San Francisco
San Diego = the southern anchor: its forge, cannon & flour
also served the Dominican frontier (C-A 9 d309, C-A 8 d399)
+ escoltas garrisoning the Franciscan missions
MISSIONS · FRANCISCAN
Apostolic College of San Fernando (Mexico City) sends the friars;
a Father-Presidente heads the chain, San Diego → San Francisco
the governor follows "the missions of the Colegio" (C-A 25 d587)
PUEBLOS
San José · Los Ángeles · Branciforte
(Baja had no civil pueblos · only the Real de Santa Ana mines)
PRESIDIO OF LORETO · the only one
the peninsula's single presidio (1697); same revistas, same
inspection & audit machine as the Alta companies (C-A 2–3)
its company detaches the frontier escoltas & the mail escort
capital of Las Californias until 1777; of Baja after 1804
COMANDANTE DE LA FRONTERA
HQ = Mission San Vicente · a lieutenant (once a mere sergeant)
commands ALL the escoltas of the Dominican frontier missions
as one district (Neve's instrucción, 1781 · C-A 2 d169)
José Manuel Ruiz held it ~1790s–1821; monthly diaries up-chain
"could aid San Diego in danger" (C-A 13 d398)
MISSIONS · DOMINICAN
the Order of Preachers holds the whole peninsula chain,
Loreto north to San Miguel, under its own Padre-Presidente
the governor follows "the missions of the Dominican fathers"
1 · THE MAIL RELAY
monthly courier: San Diego ↔ frontier ↔ mission-to-mission down the
peninsula ↔ across the Gulf ↔ Álamos / Arizpe → Mexico (C-A 2 d229, C-A 7 d2)
2 · MUTUAL AID & SUPPLY
San Diego arms & provisions the frontier; the frontier company stands
ready to reinforce San Diego (C-A 8 d399, C-A 13 d398)
3 · ONE OFFICER CORPS
careers cross the line: Goycoechea (Santa Bárbara → Gov. of Baja),
Argüello (San Francisco → Gov. of Baja) · and one Habilitado General for both
4 · ONE CHURCH PROVINCE ABOVE THE ORDERS
both halves remain in the Diocese of Sonora; the Crown's patronato
runs through each governor as "vice-patrón" · the king's local
deputy in church patronage (he appoints, funds & protects)
THE CLOSED BACK DOOR · no road east
no overland road to Sonora: prohibited by art. 115 of Gálvez's 1786
instruction (quoted C-A 11 d24); the Yumas held the Colorado crossing
after the 1781 revolt. Reconnaissances only (Arrillaga 1796, C-A 8 d148);
everything heavy for BOTH halves came by sea from San Blas
THE SEA LANE & THE PENINSULAR ROAD
San Blas ships supply both coasts; the goleta shuttles Loreto ↔ San Luis;
travellers & governors ride the mission chain (Borica 1794: Loreto →
Monterey in 4 months, inspecting 10 Dominican + 9 Fernandino houses)
San Vicente sits 250 leguas from Loreto (Arrillaga's 1796 diary)
appoints · pays · supplies
appoints · pays · supplies
vice-patrón
vice-patrón
▶ WHY SPLIT?
A Monterey government "no puede celar á distancia de 600 leguas… hasta el cabo de San Lúcas" · "cannot keep watch at a distance of 600 leagues… to Cape San Lucas" (C-A 54 d216).
And the halves faced different enemies: Alta faced FOREIGN NAVIES · after Nootka, San Francisco was "el último punto que podemos poseer… con completo é independiente dominio,"
"the last point we can hold… in complete and independent dominion" · while Baja faced DISTANCE and the desert frontier.
That is also why Alta got four presidios and Baja kept one: presidios answered ships; escoltas answered the frontier.
HOW TO READ THIS CHART
solid arrow = chain of command (appoints / issues orders / answers to)
dotted arrow = a church line of authority
blue dashed double arrow = a thread ACROSS the division · the ties that kept the halves one system
= the two governors (equal rank, parallel commands)
= the dividing line itself (a church boundary promoted to a political one)
= Church institutions (Franciscan college / Dominican province)

Companion to "Government of Spanish California 1769–1821" and "Government of Mexican California 1822–1846." Every cited record is a BANC MSS C-A document (volume + doc id), readable at archivesofcalifornia.com.
Source: Aodhan Coyne, research file "two-californias-baja-presidios-and-frontier" + leaf read of Arrillaga's 1796 diary (C-A 8 d148). Compiled 2026-10-16.
